title: Modal Perfect: Should Have, Must Have, Might Have
subtitle: Talk about the past with regret, certainty, or uncertainty.
objectives: Form the modal perfect (modal + have + past participle)
Use should have/shouldn't have for regret or criticism about the past
Use must have for a confident guess about the past
Use might have/could have for an uncertain guess about the past

content.intro: You already use must/might/should for the present and future. Add "have + past participle" and they move into the past — for regret, deduction, and uncertain guesses about what happened.

rules.heading: a) Should have / shouldn't have — regret, criticism
rules.body:
• You should have called me. (you didn't, and that was a mistake)
  • I shouldn't have eaten so much. (I did, and I regret it)

rules.heading: b) Must have — confident deduction
rules.body: • He must have left already — his car is gone. (strong evidence, confident guess)

rules.heading: c) Might have / could have — uncertain guess
rules.body:
• She might have missed the bus. (just a possibility, not certain)
  • They could have forgotten about the meeting.

examples: You should have told me earlier.
He must have forgotten his phone — it's still on the table.
She might have missed the bus.
We should have left earlier to avoid the traffic.

commonMistakes.why: The modal perfect needs the past participle (called), not the base form.
Modal verbs never change form — always "have," never "has," regardless of subject.

commonMistakes.wrong: She might had missed the bus.
commonMistakes.right: She might have missed the bus.
commonMistakes.why: The correct form is "might have," not "might had."

commonMistakes.wrong: I should have not said that.
commonMistakes.why: The negative goes as "shouldn't have," not "should have not."

exercises.title: Fill in the Blanks
exercises.instructions: Complete each sentence with the correct modal perfect form.

items.explanation: Regret/criticism about a missed action — should have + past participle.

items.prompt: He ___ (must/forget) his phone — it's still here.
items.explanation: Confident deduction from evidence — must have + past participle.

items.prompt: She ___ (might/miss) the bus. I'm not sure.
items.explanation: Uncertain guess — might have + past participle.
Regret about something that did happen — shouldn't have + past participle.

items.prompt: The lights are off and the car is gone — they ___ already.
items.explanation: Strong evidence points to a confident conclusion — "must have."

items.prompt: I don't know why she's late — she ___ traffic, or she ___ forgotten.
items.explanation: Two uncertain possibilities — "might have" for both.

items.incorrect: You should have tell me earlier.
answer: You should have told me earlier.
items.explanation: The modal perfect needs the past participle.
Modal verbs never take -s or change to "has."

summary: Should have/shouldn't have = regret or criticism about the past.
Must have = a confident deduction, based on evidence.
Might have/could have = an uncertain guess about the past.
Always: modal + have + past participle — never "has," never the base or past tense form of the main verb.
